evidence.claim: Near Chadron, the Pine Ridge adds forested buttes, ridges and canyons carved from the high tableland.
evidence.quote: The high tableland between the rivers has been eroded into a region of forested buttes, ridges and canyons.

evidence.claim: An earlier road carried supplies toward the Black Hills gold fields.
evidence.quote: It competed with the Cheyenne Black Hills Stage Route to supply the gold mining fields of the Black Hills

evidence.claim: From 1876 to 1887, the Sidney Black Hills Stage Road connected Sidney and the Union Pacific Railroad with destinations including Custer City and Deadwood.
evidence.quote: The Sidney Black Hills Stage Road or Route was a trail connecting Sidney, Nebraska, Sidney Barracks, and the Union Pacific Railroad with Fort Robinson, Red Cloud Agency, Spotted Tail Agency, Custer City, Dakota Territory, and Deadwood, Dakota Territory between 1876 and 1887, when it was replaced.

evidence.claim: It passed Courthouse and Jail Rocks and crossed the North Platte on Clarke Bridge.
evidence.quote: The trail went north from Sidney past Courthouse and Jail Rocks to present-day Bridgeport, Nebraska where it crossed the North Platte River via the Clarke Bridge

evidence.claim: Rail connections replaced the trail in 1887; the present U.S. 385 designation first appeared in 1959.
evidence.quote: prior to the construction of the Cowboy Line railroad in Northern Nebraska in 1887, which linked the Black Hills by rail to the rest of the world.

evidence.quote: Chadron State Park is a public recreation area located within the Nebraska National Forest, nine miles (14 km) south of Chadron, Nebraska

evidence.quote: Alliance is home to Carhenge, a replica of Stonehenge constructed with automobiles, which is located north of the city.

evidence.claim: Chadron moved to meet the railroad, taking its buildings along.
evidence.quote: the townspeople packed up the entire town—buildings included—and moved it to the new location.

evidence.claim: Founder Fannie O'Linn had established the community, first called O'Linn, where Chadron Creek meets the White River.
evidence.quote: Chadron was first named O'Linn for its founder Fannie O'Linn, who built a community at the confluence of the White River and Chadron Creek.

evidence.claim: That was the expected railroad branch point.
evidence.quote: This is where the railroad was expected to branch.

evidence.claim: Instead, the tracks went to Bordeaux Creek, six miles away, and the town followed.
evidence.quote: When it was built six miles away on Bordeaux Creek, the townspeople packed up the entire town—buildings included—and moved it to the new location.

evidence.claim: The city now stands amid prairie grassland, with lightly forested hills to the south.
evidence.quote: It is surrounded by prairie grassland, broken by a ridge of lightly forested hills to the south.

evidence.claim: Near Chadron, the Museum of the Fur Trade occupies the site of the American Fur Company's former Bordeaux Trading Post.
evidence.quote: The Museum of the Fur Trade is located near Chadron, at the site of the American Fur Company's former Bordeaux Trading Post.

evidence.claim: A 1962 Cadillac takes the heelstone's place at Carhenge.
evidence.quote: The heelstone is a 1962 Cadillac.

evidence.claim: Near Alliance, gray-painted American automobiles reproduce the shape of Stonehenge.
evidence.quote: Carhenge is a replica of England's Stonehenge located near the city of Alliance, Nebraska, in the High Plains region of the United States.

evidence.claim: Some cars stand trunk-down in five-foot pits; others are welded across their tops to form arches.
evidence.quote: Some are held upright in pits 5 feet (1.5 m) deep, trunk end down, and arches have been formed by welding automobiles atop the supporting models.

evidence.claim: Jim Reinders conceived the work in 1982 as a memorial to his father, who had lived on this farm.
evidence.quote: Carhenge was conceived in 1982 by Jim Reinders as a memorial to his father, who once lived on the farm now containing Carhenge.

evidence.claim: He had studied Stonehenge while living in England.
evidence.quote: While living in England, he studied the structure of Stonehenge

evidence.claim: Dedicated at the June 1987 summer solstice, the sculpture reproduces Stonehenge's surviving, incomplete form.
evidence.quote: Built by Jim Reinders, it was dedicated at the June 1987 summer solstice.

evidence.claim: gray-painted American automobiles
evidence.quote: Carhenge is formed from vintage American automobiles, all covered with gray spray paint.

evidence.claim: the sculpture reproduces Stonehenge's surviving, incomplete form.

evidence.claim: Courthouse and Jail Rocks rise 240 feet above Pumpkin Creek near Bridgeport.
evidence.quote: At an elevation of  4,050 feet (1,230 m) above sea level they rise 240 feet (73 m) above Pumpkin Creek.

evidence.claim: Their clay, sandstone and volcanic ash are remnants of an ancient plateau split by the North Platte River.
evidence.quote: Court House and Jail House Rocks are remnants of an ancient plateau, that was split by the North Platte River.

evidence.claim: The Oregon-California, Mormon, Pony Express and Sidney-Deadwood trails all passed nearby.
evidence.quote: The Oregon-California Trail, the Mormon Trail, the Pony Express Trail and the Sidney-Deadwood Trail all ran near the rocks.

evidence.claim: Travelers gave the formations architectural names: castles, a church and coffins appeared in descriptions before Courthouse and Jail became the most common.
evidence.quote: By 1849 and the California Gold Rush, the promontories had been described as Castles, a Church, and Coffins. The name Court House and Jail House became the most common.

evidence.claim: Hundreds of emigrants mentioned Courthouse Rock in their journals, recording the landmark as they traveled west.
evidence.quote: Hundreds of westward-bound emigrants mentioned Courthouse Rock (originally also McFarlan's Castle) in their travel logs and journals.

evidence.claim: near Bridgeport.
evidence.quote: Courthouse and Jail Rocks are two rock formations located near Bridgeport in the Nebraska Panhandle.

evidence.claim: Their clay, sandstone and volcanic ash
evidence.quote: are composed of Brule clay, Gering sandstone and volcanic ash.

evidence.claim: Alliance stands at the western edge of the Sand Hills.
evidence.quote: Alliance is located at the western edge of Nebraska's Sand Hills.

evidence.claim: near Courthouse and Jail Rocks
evidence.quote: Courthouse and Jail Rocks are two rock formations located near Bridgeport in the Nebraska Panhandle.

evidence.claim: The city's name honors Louis Chartran, a Métis fur trapper who ran a trading post on Chadron Creek in 1841.
evidence.quote:
Chadron is named for Louis Chartran, a French-Indian (Métis) fur trapper who ran a trading post on 
Chadron Creek in 1841.

evidence.claim: Other sculptures made from cars have since joined it on the site, now called the Car Art Reserve.
evidence.quote: Other automobile sculptures were subsequently added to the location of Carhenge, which is now known as the Car Art Reserve.

evidence.claim: Some travelers left the Oregon Trail by as much as five miles to see the rocks.
evidence.quote: Many travelers would stray as much as five miles (8 km) from the Oregon Trail just to get a glimpse of the rocks.

evidence.claim: The park is wooded with ponderosa pine, with cottonwoods near the creek and lagoon.
evidence.quote: The park is wooded with ponderosa pine throughout and cottonwood trees near the creek and lagoon.
